Day 3, 13:40 · Alex Jansen, Software Engineer, Google Shopping · coverage: transcript

Speaker matched from his self-introduction to the official speaker list. No slides were photographed.

## Claims

- **[Stage]** Google's Merchant Center feed specification is how millions of merchants send Google billions of product offers, which are used in Shopping ads, Search ads and organic search results.
  <br><sub>`D3-C352` · Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links (Alex Jansen) · not in Google docs · Used by the glossary term *Merchant Center*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Schema.org product markup on websites is another source of billions of product offers for Google Shopping, next to merchant feeds.
  <br><sub>`D3-C353` · Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links (Alex Jansen) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Product snippets in Google Search are powered by both shopping feeds and schema.org structured data.
  <br><sub>`D3-C354` · Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links (Alex Jansen) · confirmed by Google docs · [Introduction to Product structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product) · Used by `DEV-SHP-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Traditional shopping results use a small set of well-defined attributes because they take little screen space: title, image, price, perhaps star ratings, shipping cost and time, and return information; in the past that was sufficient.
  <br><sub>`D3-C355` · Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links (Alex Jansen) · consistent with Google docs · [Introduction to Product structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Behind the visible attributes, small pieces of product data such as brand and UPC or other barcodes are very important for Google Shopping's query understanding, retrieval and ranking.
  <br><sub>`D3-C356` · Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links (Alex Jansen) · consistent with Google docs · [Product data specification](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/7052112?hl=en)</sub>

- **[Stage]** In AI Mode, shoppers keep asking deeper, more nuanced follow-up questions about brands and products, so AI Mode must return much more detailed product information than classic shopping results needed.
  <br><sub>`D3-C357` · Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links (Alex Jansen) · consistent with Google docs · [AI features and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Product data quality matters more than ever for AI ('garbage in, garbage out'), and even more for agents acting on behalf of consumers, because an agent with bad data cannot do the right thing.
  > "If the agent has bad data, it cannot do the right things."
  <br><sub>`D3-C358` · Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links (Alex Jansen) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Merchants can now provide a document describing a product, such as a PDF manual, a spec sheet or the package contents, so that AI can work out what the product is about.

- **[Stage]** The related products feed attribute describes accessories, parts and replacement products, answering frequent questions such as what else to buy with a printer.

- **[Docs]** Merchant Center's popularity_rank is a 0-100 value the merchant assigns to rank a product's popularity, based on its recent sales, against the rest of its own inventory; it does not reflect user ratings.

- **[Analysis]** On stage the popularity rank was framed as how well a product sells on a marketplace, but Google's documentation defines it as the merchant's own 0-100 ranking against the rest of its inventory: a self-reported, relative value, not a sales figure across shops.

- **[Stage]** Basic product markup has two parts: product data that is the same for every merchant (name, description, brand, images) and offer data specific to one merchant's offer (URL, condition, availability, price).

- **[Stage]** In product markup, an offer's shipping and return information can point through a JSON-LD identifier (@id) to shipping and return data defined elsewhere.

- **[Stage]** Google Shopping described product data for AI as early days in a fast-moving area, with many more changes to come.
  <br><sub>`D3-C409` · Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links (Alex Jansen)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Shop developers should first keep core feed and markup values (price, availability, brand, GTIN) accurate, then add Q&As, product highlights, specs as key-value product details and related products in the Merchant Center feed, and mirror them in schema.org Product markup only as Google documents support for it.
  <br><sub>`D3-C410` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Content teams can feed the new Q&A attribute from real customer questions (support tickets, reviews, sales chats), answered factually per product; this is the detailed, merchant-owned data Google said AI shopping answers need.
  <br><sub>`D3-C411` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Shopping on Search: Beyond the blue links</sub>
